text:
sam: quick heads up — I just hit a repeatable case where the kernel picker chooses a non-causal SDPA path during causal streaming, only when head_dim % 16 == 0 but not % 32. reproducer attached below.
maria: hmm that sounds bad. which model / seq len / hw? can you paste the picker output?
eugene: saw something similar on nightly. here's a short dump from the picker + perf counters (trimmed):
```
[picker] model: llama-small, seq=256, head_dim=48, layers=32
[hw] arch=sm86, gpu_mem=48GB
[picker] candidates: flash_v3_causal(head=48)->score=78, sdpa_v2_noncausal(head=48)->score=82
[picker] final: sdpa_v2_noncausal chosen (heuristic: raw_throughput_est)
[perf] observed latency bump +12% vs expected causal flash path
```
sam: key bit is picker scoring prefers throughput estimate and doesn't re-evaluate correctness for 'causal' flag in some quant/tiling combos. result = chosen kernel can't handle reversed kv-cache update ordering -> we fall back at runtime and pay huge penalty.
rachel: interesting — on h100 (sm90) we have different tiling so fallback cost is smaller, but on sm86 it basically forces a slowpath. i think the root is the scoring model not incorporating 'kv-ordering-safe' attribute.
maria: can we add a gate so any candidate marked non-causal is ineligible for requests where request.meta.causal==true? should be quick.
eugene: quick note: it's not just tagged non-causal. sdpa_v2 has a variant that *can* be configured causal with an extra pad-unroll; our picker doesn't model that binary param. so we either need to expand candidate space (sdpa_v2_causal, sdpa_v2_noncausal) or add a post-filter check.
perf-bot: perf trace uploaded: https://perf.redwood.internal/traces/2024/1737654321 (contains before/after microbench)
sam: repro steps i used:
1) start inference with streaming=true, causal=true
2) model config head_dim=48, seq=256, microbatch=1
3) run ~1000 requests to warmup
4) observe stochastic picks in logs: "selected sdpa_v2_noncausal"
maria: sounds good. i'll try expand candidate enumeration to include a causal-flagged sdpa variant and run autotune sweep for head_dim buckets (16/32/48/64). if we expand candidates, picker search space jumps; we should limit to arch-specific combos.
eugene: i can repro locally and push a minimal patch to add a post-filter that removes kernels that lack kv-ordering-safe for causal requests. that buys us time while maria runs a proper autotune.
rachel: also check batching heuristics: some microbatch shapes cause head_dim alignment to change tile selection. batching+pad noise might flip the mod-based heuristics. worth testing with and without prefix-caching.
sam: priority: P2. impact: certain customer streaming workloads see 10-30% latency regression. owner: maria + eugene. next: maria will run autotune (1737658000 window), eugene will land the post-filter PR and add a unit test to cover picks for causal flag.
maria: adding to my board. i'll post results in this thread when sweep finishes. :white_check_mark:
eugene: created draft PR: https://git.redwood/infer/kernel-picker/pulls/412 - includes filter + small logger for rejected candidates.
sam: thanks. if either of you finds the picker score model needs retraining, file an infra jobs ticket so we can run a quick calibration on the nightly traces.
perf-bot: autotune sweep scheduled: 2024-11-14T03:00:00Z for arch=sm86,sm90. results will be posted to /schedules/1737654321-autotune
maria: copied. i'll ping infra if we need extra GPUs.
sam: nice work team. follow-ups: (1) short-term filter (eugene) (2) enumerate causal-capable variants (maria) (3) add unit/regression capturing picker output for head_dim in CI (both). closing loop once autotune + PR are in.
rachel: fyi i'll also add a note to the rollout playbook about checking "kv-ordering-safe" before canarying any picker change. saved us once. :memo:
eugene: one more microdetail: when head_dim==48 we should bias towards flash_v3_causal if seq <= 384 on sm86. i'll add that heuristic to the patch as a temporary tie-breaker.
sam: perfect. thumbs up. :thumbsup:
